wv_03_double_tier_wall.blurb: Double-Tier Wall is a cliff band in the Bozoo cluster of southern West Virginia, sitting beside Simpson Wall along the trail leaving the Shanklin's Ferry campground. It holds eleven routes on sandstone, almost all of them trad with a single top-rope line. Grades start at 5.6 and stretch to the low 5.12s, though most of the leads fall between 5.8 and 5.10, with a few hard test pieces for strong climbers. It is a compact wall that suits a rack-and-rope day, and it pairs naturally with the neighboring walls.

wv_09_white_wall.blurb: White Wall is a southeast-facing cliff band in the Bozoo cluster of southern West Virginia, among the upstream walls that include the Iceberg and Savory areas. Cliffs run roughly 65 feet tall and pick up plenty of sun. The eleven routes are mostly trad, with a few top-rope lines and one sport route, on sandstone. Grades span 5.8 up to the 5.11s, with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, making it a fair choice for a climber comfortable leading on gear and wanting some steadier moderates.

wv_ali_bubba_cave.blurb: Ali Bubba Cave is a steep bouldering cave at Beauty Mountain, part of the Short Creek boulders near Fayetteville in the New River Gorge. The eleven problems here are mostly hard: a couple of V3 and V4 warm-ups, then a strong block of V7 to V10 lines on sandstone. What sets the cave apart is that it stays climbable in the rain, needing essentially no drying time, so it is the usual fallback on wet days. The wider Short Creek zone is best from fall through spring and catches plenty of winter sun.

wv_f_flash_point_area.blurb: Flash Point Area is a short stretch of the Endless Wall in the New River Gorge, lying between Diamond Point and the Kaymoor Slabs. It holds eleven routes on sandstone, a fairly even split of six sport and five trad. The grades start near 5.7 and rise through a good run of 5.10 and 5.11 lines to a few 5.12s and beyond, so it leans toward intermediate and strong climbers rather than beginners. Most people arrive by going down the Honeymooner's ladders and then walking downstream along the base.
